stem: Vikram describes the same shaded rectangle of width $4$ and length $x+5$ in two ways: $4(x+5)$ and $4x+20$.

options.text: Expanding $4(x+5)$ gives $4x+20$, so the two expressions are equivalent for the same rectangle.
The expressions are equivalent even when they describe different widths.
Having $4x+20$ produces the partition $4(x+5)$, so expansion is unnecessary to test equivalence.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Both expressions describe the same rectangle, and distributive expansion shows $4(x+5)=4x+20$.

teacher.key_rationale: Same whole under the same meanings: expand 4(x+5) to 4x+20. Dropping shared dimensions, or treating the expanded form as creating the partition, misses the equivalence hinge.
